**4. Adoption of the Constitution**
The draft constitution, which had been circulated to all present prior to the meeting, was read out clause by clause by the Recording Secretary.

- **Clause 1 (Name):** The Association shall be known as the Tan Family Association.
- **Clause 2 (Objectives):** The objectives of the Association shall be to promote unity and mutual assistance among members of the Tan clan; to provide financial aid, education, and welfare support to members in need; to preserve and honour the traditions and customs of the Tan clan; and to foster good relations with other clan associations in Singapore.
- **Clause 3 (Membership):** Membership shall be open to all persons of the Tan surname, male and female, aged 18 and above, who are of good character and who agree to abide by the rules of the Association.
- **Clause 4 (Subscription):** The monthly subscription shall be fixed at fifty cents per member. An entrance fee of one dollar shall be payable upon admission.
- **Clause 5 (Management Committee):** The affairs of the Association shall be managed by a Management Committee comprising a Chairman, Vice-Chairman, Honorary Secretary, Honorary Treasurer, and six ordinary committee members. The Committee shall be elected at the Annual General Meeting and shall hold office for a term of two years.
- **Clause 6 (Meetings):** The Annual General Meeting shall be held in the month of March each year. Ordinary meetings of the Management Committee shall be held monthly. A special general meeting may be convened by the Chairman or upon the written request of at least ten members.
- **Clause 7 (Finance):** The funds of the Association shall be deposited in a bank account in the name of the Association. All cheques shall be signed by the Honorary Treasurer and countersigned by the Chairman or Vice-Chairman.
- **Clause 8 (Amendments):** This constitution may be amended only by a resolution passed by a two-thirds majority of members present at a general meeting, provided that notice of the proposed amendment has been given in writing at least fourteen days prior to the meeting.

A general discussion followed. Mr. Tan Boon Leong proposed that an additional clause be inserted to allow for the establishment of a scholarship fund for the education of members' children. This was seconded by Mr. Tan Gim Huat. The Chairman ruled that this proposal be noted and referred to the incoming Management Committee for further study, as it would require careful financial planning.

The constitution as read was then put to the vote. It was carried unanimously.

The founding documents of the Tan Family Association record that it was founded_on 1923-03-15. Record status: current.

The name of the association shall be the Tan Family Association, hereinafter referred to as "the Association." In Chinese, it shall be known as 新加坡陈氏公会. The registered office of the Association shall be at 12 Amoy Street, Singapore, or at such other place as the Committee may from time to time determine with the approval of the Registrar of Societies.

ARTICLE II — OBJECTS

The objects of the Association shall be:

(a) To promote fellowship and unity among persons of the Tan surname resident in the Straits Settlements and the Malay States;

(b) To provide financial and other assistance to members who are in distress, sickness, or need, subject to the rules hereinafter contained;

(c) To establish and maintain a fund for the education of the children of members;

(d) To acquire, hold, and manage property, both movable and immovable, for the purposes of the Association;

(e) To organize and conduct ancestral worship ceremonies and other cultural activities in accordance with Chinese tradition;

(f) To foster good relations with other clan associations and charitable institutions in Singapore.

ARTICLE III — MEMBERSHIP

Section 1. Membership shall be open to any person of the Tan surname, male or female, who is of good character and who is resident in the Straits Settlements or the Malay States.

Section 2. Application for membership shall be made in writing to the Secretary, and shall be proposed by one member and seconded by another. The Committee shall have power to accept or reject any application without assigning any reason therefor.

Section 3. There shall be the following classes of members:

(a) Ordinary Members — persons who pay the entrance fee and annual subscription;

(b) Life Members — persons who have paid a single sum of fifty dollars ($50.00) in lieu of all future subscriptions;

(c) Honorary Members — persons who have rendered distinguished service to the Association or to the community, and who have been elected by the General Meeting upon the recommendation of the Committee.

Section 4. The rights and privileges of members shall be personal to them and shall not be transferable.

ARTICLE IV — ENTRANCE FEES AND SUBSCRIPTIONS

The Registry of Societies registration_number is ROS-1923-0045 as per the registration documents. Record status: current.

Section 1. The entrance fee shall be five dollars ($5.00) for ordinary members and ten dollars ($10.00) for life members.

Section 2. The annual subscription shall be two dollars ($2.00), payable in advance on the first day of January of each year.

Section 3. Any member whose subscription remains unpaid for a period of twelve months shall cease to be entitled to the benefits of the Association, and shall be deemed to have resigned if the arrears remain unpaid after due notice in writing from the Secretary.

ARTICLE V — MANAGEMENT

Section 1. The affairs of the Association shall be managed by a Committee consisting of:

(a) President
(b) Vice-President
(c) Honorary Secretary
(d) Honorary Treasurer
(e) Six (6) Committee Members

Section 2. The Committee shall be elected at the Annual General Meeting and shall hold office for a term of one year, from the first day of January to the thirty-first day of December.

Section 3. The Committee shall meet at least once a month. Five members shall form a quorum.

Section 4. The Committee shall have power to:

(a) Administer the funds and property of the Association;

(b) Appoint such sub-committees as may be necessary;

(c) Fill any casual vacancy in the Committee until the next Annual General Meeting;

(d) Authorize expenditure not exceeding fifty dollars ($50.00) without reference to the General Meeting.

ARTICLE VI — DUTIES OF OFFICERS

Section 1. The President shall preside at all meetings of the Association and of the Committee. He shall regulate the proceedings and shall have a casting vote in the event of an equality of votes.

Section 2. The Vice-President shall perform the duties of the President in his absence.

Section 3. The Honorary Secretary shall keep the minutes of all meetings, conduct the correspondence of the Association, have custody of the seal and records, and shall submit a report of the activities of the Association at the Annual General Meeting.
ARTICLE VI — DUTIES OF OFFICERS (continued)

Section 4. The Honorary Treasurer shall receive all moneys belonging to the Association, shall keep proper accounts of all receipts and expenditure, and shall present a statement of accounts at the Annual General Meeting. All cheques shall be signed by the Honorary Treasurer and countersigned by the President or the Honorary Secretary.

Section 5. The Committee Members shall attend meetings of the Committee and assist in the conduct of the affairs of the Association as the Committee may direct.

ARTICLE VII — MEETINGS

Section 1. The Annual General Meeting of the Association shall be held in the month of January in each year at such time and place as the Committee may appoint.

Section 2. Notice of the Annual General Meeting shall be given in writing to every member at least fourteen (14) days before the date of the meeting.

Section 3. The business of the Annual General Meeting shall include:

(a) The reading and confirmation of the minutes of the previous Annual General Meeting;

(b) The consideration of the report of the Committee and the statement of accounts;

(c) The election of the Committee for the ensuing year;

(d) The appointment of an Auditor;

(e) The transaction of any other business of which due notice has been given.

Section 4. Extraordinary General Meetings may be convened at any time by the President, or by the Committee, and shall be convened upon a requisition in writing signed by not less than ten (10) members, stating the object of the meeting. No business other than that stated in the requisition shall be transacted at such meeting.

Section 5. At all General Meetings, ten (10) members present in person shall form a quorum. If a quorum is not present within half an hour after the time appointed for the meeting, the meeting shall stand adjourned to the same day in the following week at the same time and place, and if at such adjourned meeting a quorum is not present within half an hour after the time appointed, the members present shall form a quorum.

Section 6. Each member present in person shall have one vote, and voting shall be by show of hands unless a ballot is demanded by not less than five (5) members. The Chairman shall have a casting vote in addition to his own vote.

ARTICLE VIII — AUDIT

Section 1. An Auditor shall be appointed at each Annual General Meeting, who shall not be a member of the Committee. The Auditor shall audit the accounts of the Association for the preceding year and shall certify to the correctness of the statement of accounts submitted to the Annual General Meeting.

Section 2. The Auditor shall be entitled to inspect all books and accounts of the Association and to require from any officer such information as may be necessary for the performance of his duties.

ARTICLE IX — FUNDS AND PROPERTY

Section 1. The funds of the Association shall be deposited in a bank to be selected by the Committee, in the name of the Association.

Section 2. No part of the funds of the Association shall be applied, directly or indirectly, to the payment of any remuneration to any member of the Committee, save for reasonable out-of-pocket expenses incurred in the discharge of their duties.

Section 3. The property of the Association shall be vested in the Committee, who shall hold the same upon trust for the Association and shall deal with the same in accordance with the resolutions of the General Meeting.

ARTICLE X — AMENDMENTS

Section 1. These Rules may be amended, added to, or repealed by a resolution passed by a majority of not less than two-thirds of the members present and voting at an Annual General Meeting or an Extraordinary General Meeting convened for that purpose.

Section 2. Notice of any proposed amendment shall be given in writing to the Honorary Secretary at least twenty-one (21) days before the date of the meeting, and notice of such proposed amendment shall be forwarded by the Honorary Secretary to every member together with the notice of the meeting.

**4. Adoption of the Constitution**
The draft constitution, which had been circulated to all present prior to the meeting, was read out clause by clause by the Recording Secretary.

- **Clause 1 (Name):** The Association shall be known as the Tan Family Association.
- **Clause 2 (Objectives):** The objectives of the Association shall be to promote unity and mutual assistance among members of the Tan clan; to provide financial aid, education, and welfare support to members in need; to preserve and honour the traditions and customs of the Tan clan; and to foster good relations with other clan associations in Singapore.
- **Clause 3 (Membership):** Membership shall be open to all persons of the Tan surname, male and female, aged 18 and above, who are of good character and who agree to abide by the rules of the Association.
- **Clause 4 (Subscription):** The monthly subscription shall be fixed at fifty cents per member. An entrance fee of one dollar shall be payable upon admission.
- **Clause 5 (Management Committee):** The affairs of the Association shall be managed by a Management Committee comprising a Chairman, Vice-Chairman, Honorary Secretary, Honorary Treasurer, and six ordinary committee members. The Committee shall be elected at the Annual General Meeting and shall hold office for a term of two years.
- **Clause 6 (Meetings):** The Annual General Meeting shall be held in the month of March each year. Ordinary meetings of the Management Committee shall be held monthly. A special general meeting may be convened by the Chairman or upon the written request of at least ten members.
- **Clause 7 (Finance):** The funds of the Association shall be deposited in a bank account in the name of the Association. All cheques shall be signed by the Honorary Treasurer and countersigned by the Chairman or Vice-Chairman.
- **Clause 8 (Amendments):** This constitution may be amended only by a resolution passed by a two-thirds majority of members present at a general meeting, provided that notice of the proposed amendment has been given in writing at least fourteen days prior to the meeting.

A general discussion followed. Mr. Tan Boon Leong proposed that an additional clause be inserted to allow for the establishment of a scholarship fund for the education of members' children. This was seconded by Mr. Tan Gim Huat. The Chairman ruled that this proposal be noted and referred to the incoming Management Committee for further study, as it would require careful financial planning.

The constitution as read was then put to the vote. It was carried unanimously.

He thanked the members for their support over the years and expressed his confidence in the ability of the incoming Committee to carry on the work of the Association.

> **Resolution No. 1/1945-46**

The resolution was put to the meeting and carried unanimously. The minutes and obituary note that Tan Ah Kow's presidency_ended on 1945-12-31. Record status: historical.

documents.content:
The name of the association shall be the Tan Family Association, hereinafter referred to as "the Association." In Chinese, it shall be known as 新加坡陈氏公会. The registered office of the Association shall be at 12 Amoy Street, Singapore, or at such other place as the Committee may from time to time determine with the approval of the Registrar of Societies.

ARTICLE II — OBJECTS

The objects of the Association shall be:

(a) To promote fellowship and unity among persons of the Tan surname resident in the Straits Settlements and the Malay States;

(b) To provide financial and other assistance to members who are in distress, sickness, or need, subject to the rules hereinafter contained;

(c) To establish and maintain a fund for the education of the children of members;

(d) To acquire, hold, and manage property, both movable and immovable, for the purposes of the Association;

(e) To organize and conduct ancestral worship ceremonies and other cultural activities in accordance with Chinese tradition;

(f) To foster good relations with other clan associations and charitable institutions in Singapore.

ARTICLE III — MEMBERSHIP

Section 1. Membership shall be open to any person of the Tan surname, male or female, who is of good character and who is resident in the Straits Settlements or the Malay States.

Section 2. Application for membership shall be made in writing to the Secretary, and shall be proposed by one member and seconded by another. The Committee shall have power to accept or reject any application without assigning any reason therefor.

Section 3. There shall be the following classes of members:

(a) Ordinary Members — persons who pay the entrance fee and annual subscription;

(b) Life Members — persons who have paid a single sum of fifty dollars ($50.00) in lieu of all future subscriptions;

(c) Honorary Members — persons who have rendered distinguished service to the Association or to the community, and who have been elected by the General Meeting upon the recommendation of the Committee.

Section 4. The rights and privileges of members shall be personal to them and shall not be transferable.

ARTICLE IV — ENTRANCE FEES AND SUBSCRIPTIONS

Section 1. The entrance fee shall be five dollars ($5.00) for ordinary members and ten dollars ($10.00) for life members.

Section 2. The annual subscription shall be two dollars ($2.00), payable in advance on the first day of January of each year.

Section 3. Any member whose subscription remains unpaid for a period of twelve months shall cease to be entitled to the benefits of the Association, and shall be deemed to have resigned if the arrears remain unpaid after due notice in writing from the Secretary.

ARTICLE V — MANAGEMENT

Section 1. The affairs of the Association shall be managed by a Committee consisting of:

(a) President
(b) Vice-President
(c) Honorary Secretary
(d) Honorary Treasurer
(e) Six (6) Committee Members

Section 2. The Committee shall be elected at the Annual General Meeting and shall hold office for a term of one year, from the first day of January to the thirty-first day of December.

Section 3. The Committee shall meet at least once a month. Five members shall form a quorum.

Section 4. The Committee shall have power to:

(a) Administer the funds and property of the Association;

(b) Appoint such sub-committees as may be necessary;

(c) Fill any casual vacancy in the Committee until the next Annual General Meeting;

(d) Authorize expenditure not exceeding fifty dollars ($50.00) without reference to the General Meeting.

ARTICLE VI — DUTIES OF OFFICERS

Section 1. The President shall preside at all meetings of the Association and of the Committee. He shall regulate the proceedings and shall have a casting vote in the event of an equality of votes.

Section 2. The Vice-President shall perform the duties of the President in his absence.

Section 3. The Honorary Secretary shall keep the minutes of all meetings, conduct the correspondence of the Association, have custody of the seal and records, and shall submit a report of the activities of the Association at the Annual General Meeting.

ARTICLE VI — DUTIES OF OFFICERS (continued)

Section 4. The Honorary Treasurer shall receive all moneys belonging to the Association, shall keep proper accounts of all receipts and expenditure, and shall present a statement of accounts at the Annual General Meeting. All cheques shall be signed by the Honorary Treasurer and countersigned by the President or the Honorary Secretary.

Section 5. The Committee Members shall attend meetings of the Committee and assist in the conduct of the affairs of the Association as the Committee may direct.

ARTICLE VII — MEETINGS

Section 1. The Annual General Meeting of the Association shall be held in the month of January in each year at such time and place as the Committee may appoint.

Section 2. Notice of the Annual General Meeting shall be given in writing to every member at least fourteen (14) days before the date of the meeting.

Section 3. The business of the Annual General Meeting shall include:

(a) The reading and confirmation of the minutes of the previous Annual General Meeting;

(b) The consideration of the report of the Committee and the statement of accounts;

(c) The election of the Committee for the ensuing year;

(d) The appointment of an Auditor;

(e) The transaction of any other business of which due notice has been given.

Section 4. Extraordinary General Meetings may be convened at any time by the President, or by the Committee, and shall be convened upon a requisition in writing signed by not less than ten (10) members, stating the object of the meeting. No business other than that stated in the requisition shall be transacted at such meeting.

Section 5. At all General Meetings, ten (10) members present in person shall form a quorum. If a quorum is not present within half an hour after the time appointed for the meeting, the meeting shall stand adjourned to the same day in the following week at the same time and place, and if at such adjourned meeting a quorum is not present within half an hour after the time appointed, the members present shall form a quorum.

Section 6. Each member present in person shall have one vote, and voting shall be by show of hands unless a ballot is demanded by not less than five (5) members. The Chairman shall have a casting vote in addition to his own vote.

ARTICLE VIII — AUDIT

Section 1. An Auditor shall be appointed at each Annual General Meeting, who shall not be a member of the Committee. The Auditor shall audit the accounts of the Association for the preceding year and shall certify to the correctness of the statement of accounts submitted to the Annual General Meeting.

Section 2. The Auditor shall be entitled to inspect all books and accounts of the Association and to require from any officer such information as may be necessary for the performance of his duties.

ARTICLE IX — FUNDS AND PROPERTY

Section 1. The funds of the Association shall be deposited in a bank to be selected by the Committee, in the name of the Association.

Section 2. No part of the funds of the Association shall be applied, directly or indirectly, to the payment of any remuneration to any member of the Committee, save for reasonable out-of-pocket expenses incurred in the discharge of their duties.

Section 3. The property of the Association shall be vested in the Committee, who shall hold the same upon trust for the Association and shall deal with the same in accordance with the resolutions of the General Meeting.

ARTICLE X — AMENDMENTS

Section 1. These Rules may be amended, added to, or repealed by a resolution passed by a majority of not less than two-thirds of the members present and voting at an Annual General Meeting or an Extraordinary General Meeting convened for that purpose.

Section 2. Notice of any proposed amendment shall be given in writing to the Honorary Secretary at least twenty-one (21) days before the date of the meeting, and notice of such proposed amendment shall be forwarded by the Honorary Secretary to every member together with the notice of the meeting.
